patch.value: Extend native ownership to selection and composed lifecycle commands

Follow up explicit claim/release parity with claim --next, claim --start, release --pause, detected session principals and extension/semantic attribution integration; preserve published compound-operation failure receipts.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Follow-up boundary from pm-rust-zukw: explicit asserted-author ownership is implemented with CLI 2026.10.7 differential coverage. Selection, composed start/pause operations, detected session principals, extension bypass and semantic attribution remain separate work.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Additional documented boundary: the native explicit ownership surface emits compact JSON receipts; alternate published rendering formats remain follow-up work alongside selection, composed lifecycle operations and session attribution.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Implement native selection and composed ownership lifecycle using existing mutation transactions; characterize published 2026.10.13 output, session principals, attribution and partial-failure receipts with real scratch trackers. Include adjacent comment and tag ordering parity fixes when shared normalization is involved.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Oracle confirms composed start uses claim then update, and pause uses update then release; each is an independent durable mutation. Detected identity principals hash the harness and session signals. Native selection will filter ready work then retry only foreign-claim conflicts under existing per-item locks.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Initial exact-byte checks exposed JSON refusal key order, omitted provenance dimensions, session-state replacement and recursive array patch differences. Corrected those contract details. Clippy passes with warnings denied; focused comparisons are running in an isolated HOME and Git environment.

value.author: codex-agent

Each function was restored exactly. Two lifecycle/refusal details found in the broader run have also been corrected; final positive-control gates are next.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Native selection, session principals, default human/gate classification, SDK release bypass, ordering fixes, fixed-clock item/history bytes, and a two-process claim-next race pass their oracle scenarios. Pre-existing malformed-ID lock writes are tracked separately as pm-rust-2tb9.

value.author: codex-agent

value.author: codex-agent

Added readiness, dependency-cycle, structural-ranking, attribution, recursive-patch and validation regressions. The candidate published 2026.10.14 oracle is under test before any lockfile adoption; initial version-guard failures were expected while the declared contract remained 2026.10.13.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Confirmed and fixed a review finding: lifecycle ignored schema.files.workflows when type_workflows existed only in the external schema. The strengthened real-tracker failed-start test compiled and failed at runtime (native exit 0 versus oracle exit 2) before the fix, then passed with exact bytes after a shared native runtime-schema loader was added. Selection now uses that loader for external status roles as well.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Candidate oracle acceptance: all six existing differential suites passed against published 2026.10.14 (41 tests: branch merge 1, ownership 14, conformance 2, list 8, output 2, pagination 14). The added external-status regression also passed. Adopting 2026.10.14 in the committed oracle lock and advertised compatibility constant; full final-tree release gates remain pending.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Fresh behavioral revert verification against the locked 2026.10.14 oracle: disabling only claim_next, removing only the composed start step, reverting only tag locale sorting, and reverting only comment tie ordering each compiled and produced exactly one runtime regression failure (exit 101). Every production source was restored byte for byte. The external-workflow regression separately failed before its native schema-loader repair and passed afterward.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: The combined parent/metadata/ownership differential exposed an inherited selection mismatch: published assignee-filter accepts assigned|unassigned and refuses mine, while native accepted mine and ignored assigned. Corrected the supported filter and preserved the exact invalid-value JSON refusal. The regression retains both the invalid mine case and valid assigned selection; final-tree gate reruns will include this repair.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: The cross-session selection regression exposed a published identity handoff quirk: claim-next forwards the detected display author as asserted identity to each atomic claim. An unclaimed selection stores the display principal, while explicit detected claims store the session hash; even the same detected session cannot reclaim that explicit claim through selection. Native now preserves these observable bytes and exhaustion receipts. The expanded detected-session differential passes; the oracle quirk will be reported without filing upstream changes.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Both full toolchain runs passed 268 tests, including all 16 ownership/selection/lifecycle cases. The unchanged release gate correctly refused the measured coverage gap: lines 99.87468671679198, functions 100, regions 99.61506736321144, branches 98.04526748971193. Added focused cases for partial session metadata, malformed principal suffixes, focus-only worksets, permissive/no-op workflows, SDK selection options and refusal dispatch. Replaced a redundant JSON-object guard with a typed object state boundary. A new ambiguous-start case also exposed a rejected-value envelope mismatch; published probes confirm shared author/JSON controls must be omitted.

value.author: codex-agent

All four pass. These complement the 16 black-box oracle scenarios and directly verify the exported consumer API.

value.author: codex-agent

Workflow validation now uses explicit early returns for unconstrained and idempotent cases; existing refusal text and ordering are preserved. Final coverage is being rebuilt cleanly before the full aggregate rerun.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Round 1: read all five PR 77 review threads at head 582c1d1. Verify each against the pinned TypeScript oracle, retain oracle parity on disagreements, add targeted regressions and independent behavioural revert proofs, then run stable/MSRV release gates and four-dimensional coverage before delivery.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Finding 1 valid; reviewer skip suggestion disagrees with oracle. Node process.env decodes invalid UTF-8 lossily, including PM_AUTHOR. vars_os plus lossy conversion preserves that behavior. Unix differential passes for invalid key, unrelated invalid value, and PM_AUTHOR invalid value across claim/release, comparing exit/stdout/stderr and item/history/session bytes. Reverting only environment collection to vars(), rebuilding, and rerunning the exact targeted command fails: native exit 101 versus oracle 0 (1 failed); restored fix passes (1 passed).

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Oracle decisions: core/session/session-state.js calls acquireLock with force=false and forceRequiredForStaleLock=true; expired session locks are refused, so the proposed automatic recovery must not be applied. sdk/lifecycle/task-composition.js rejects ifAvailable=true before reading settings or claiming, contrary to the suggested skipped start receipt. Add real stale-lock and SDK invalid-input differentials to freeze these oracle contracts.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Finding 2 rejected for oracle parity. Real expired session-state.lock files are retained and claim/release fail in both SDKs even with ownership policy none; durable item/history/session bytes match. Targeted differential: 1 passed. Applying only the reviewer false-to-true recovery proposal fails the test (native succeeds instead of refusing; 1 failed), then restored original policy. No recovery fix exists to revert. Separate existing diagnostic mismatch is tracked in pm-rust-sldg.
